title: Service Standards for Open Medical Records Requests
content:
Four service standards apply to Medical Records Requests: status updates, portal availability, identity verification and the span of dates one request covers.

1. **Status updates.** Requesters get a status update every status-update interval of the request type, counted in business days, while the request is open.
2. **Portal availability.** Portal records become available the request type's portal availability period, in hours, after the note or result is finalized.
3. **Identity before compilation.** Where the request type requires identity verification, the requester's identity is verified before compilation starts.
4. **Span of dates per request.** One request covers at most the type's largest span of dates of service, in years; a longer span needs a second request.

## Standards restated as condition and result

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| The request is open | A status update goes to the requester at each interval of the type's business days |
| A note or result is finalized | It becomes available in the portal the type's number of hours later |
| The type requires identity verification | Compilation does not start until the requester's identity is verified |
| The dates of service asked for span more than the type's largest span | One request covers at most that span; the remainder needs a second request |

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

On a hypothetical request type that allows a span of 10 years, a requester asking for dates of service running over 14 years has at most 10 of those years covered by one request; the remaining 4 years need a second request. A span of exactly 10 years fits within one request.
